econ-econ-01-c3.claim: Under 1–5, OLS is BLUE, the Best Linear Unbiased Estimator (lowest variance among unbiased linear estimators).

econ-econ-02-c2.text: (2016). American Statistical Association Releases Statement on Statistical Significance and P-Values.
econ-econ-02-c2.quote: A p-value, or statistical significance, does not measure the size of an effect or the importance of a result.
econ-econ-02-c2.claim: Statistical significance is about whether the effect is distinguishable from noise, not whether the effect is large or important.

econ-econ-02-c5.claim: This practice, sometimes called p-hacking or 'specification searching', has been a major source of irreproducible results across social sciences.

econ-econ-05-c3.text: Justin McCrary (2007). Manipulation of the Running Variable in the Regression Discontinuity Design: A Density Test. NBER Technical Working Paper 0334.

econ-econ-05-c3.claim: RD requires that potential outcomes be continuous at the threshold.

econ-econ-05-c3.text: Justin McCrary (2007). Manipulation of the Running Variable in the Regression Discontinuity Design: A Density Test. NBER Technical Working Paper 0334.

econ-econ-05-c3.claim: The McCrary test: examine the density of the running variable at the cutoff.

econ-econ-06-c1.text: Christoph Hanck, Martin Arnold, Alexander Gerber, Martin Schmelzer. 10 Regression with Panel Data. Introduction to Econometrics with R.
econ-econ-06-c1.quote: Regression using panel data may mitigate omitted variable bias when there is no information on variables that correlate with both the regressors of interest and the dependent variable and if these variables are constant in the time dimension or across entities.
econ-econ-06-c1.claim: This separation lets you control for stable individual characteristics that you can't observe.

econ-econ-06-c2.text: Christoph Hanck, Martin Arnold, Alexander Gerber, Martin Schmelzer. 10.3 Fixed Effects Regression. Introduction to Econometrics with R.
econ-econ-06-c2.quote: Although including state fixed effects eliminates the risk of a bias due to omitted factors that vary across states but not over time, we suspect that there are other omitted variables that vary over time and thus cause a bias.
econ-econ-06-c2.claim: This dramatically reduces omitted variable bias from time-invariant confounders.
